## 761a24339019

Concrete partial-stamp counterexample. With `seed=6`, `sample_index=6`, and `difficulty="easy"`, the generator emits:

```text
0000000000
0133000000
3330000000
0000000000
0000000000
0000000000
0000000001
0000000000
```

The exemplar anchor is at `(1,1)` and its five green offsets are `(0,1)`, `(0,2)`, `(1,1)`, `(1,0)`, `(1,-1)`. The target is at `(6,9)`. Three translated positions—`(6,10)`, `(6,11)`, and `(7,10)`—are outside the 8×10 grid. The actual canonical Racket execution therefore produces only two new green cells:

```text
0000000000
0133000000
3330000000
0000000000
0000000000
0000000000
0000000001
0000000033
```

This conflicts with the generator summary/invariant that the exemplar shape is stamped at every target and introduces a boundary-clipping behavior absent from the canonical demonstrations. Target placement checks only that the marker itself and its 8-neighborhood are empty; it never checks the full translated offset set for bounds or collisions. A target should be accepted only when every exemplar offset is in bounds and lands on background (and, for multiple targets, does not collide with another planned stamp).

triage.reason: Both source-bound finding sections retained for future task owners. Local main-generator checks do not independently reproduce these audits. See REVIEW/intake-20261002-batch12.json.

## 761a24339019

### Reproduced domain defect — generated motif stamps are partially clipped

The assigned generator SHA-256
`19221bfe621e6132cb8c05ff7911b9e4342bbc18a97ba1ce5b79f1316cceba90`
reproduces a target whose full exemplar stamp does not fit the canvas. The
selected source was not edited.

For seed `6`, sample index `6`, difficulty `easy`, the generated grid is `8×10`,
passes `self_check` with `[]`, and has exemplar anchor `(1,1)` with offsets
`(0,1)`, `(0,2)`, `(1,-1)`, `(1,0)`, `(1,1)`. The target at `(6,9)` translates
three cells out of bounds: `(6,10)`, `(6,11)`, and `(7,10)`.

I executed the supported Racket authority on that exact generated input. It
exited successfully under rule hash `ea6f2120f432` and clips the translated
stamp, adding only the in-bounds green cells `(7,8)` and `(7,9)`. Thus the
validator accepts an ordinary generated case whose semantic operation is a
partial motif rather than a complete copy. This is a reproduced generator-domain
question/defect; it is not evidence that the selected Racket implementation is
internally inconsistent.

Evidence:

- `checks/audit/761a24339019/probe.json`
- `checks/audit/761a24339019/input.json`
- `checks/audit/761a24339019/racket.json`
- `checks/audit/761a24339019/racket-run.log`

Suggested repair: constrain target anchors so every translated exemplar offset
is in bounds, or explicitly document and test clipping as part of the intended
task. If complete stamping is intended, add a validator assertion and a
regression for this exact seed/sample.
